summary: danger-full-access no longer loses the Session workspace identity: resolveKernelLaunch returns a real KernelLaunch (plain interpreter argv + policy.workspaceRoot cwd) instead of undefined, marked confined=false. KernelLaunch gained a confined flag; the M9 chunked checkpoint transport (checkpoint_chunk guard, onResult, evalCell) now requires confined===true so an unconfined danger launch keeps the legacy M5 file-path transport, and sandbox error classification no longer mislabels danger launches.

pointers: Issue#87 danger-full-access keeps the Session workspace cwd
Issue#87 workspace identity stable across mode change

steps: Verified the bug at 5a1b6e1: resolveKernelLaunch returned undefined for danger-full-access, so spawn cwd and evalFrame.cwd were omitted and the kernel stayed in the Host working directory.
Introduced KernelLaunch.confined and threaded it through the three chunked-transport conditions plus spawn/exit error classification.
Regressions prove os.getcwd() and a relative write land in the workspace root with confine() never called, and a workspace-write->reset->danger mode change keeps the same cwd.

evidence.target: tests/rlm-loop.test.ts Issue#87 (2 new tests) + existing M9 suite
evidence.note: 11/11 pass incl. all M9 Issue#42 tests

limitations: The confined flag is internal; existing KernelLaunch consumers in tests construct no launch object, so this is covered only through the sandbox policy path.
